text:
maria: FYI — customer reported repeated card declines when trying to pay invoice #INV-9242. Error from PSP shows AVS/CVV/address mismatch. Attaching logs below.

sam: Can you paste the exact PSP error and charge id? Also country and billing address they used? :eyes:

maria: Stripe webhook payload excerpt: 
```
{"id":"ch_3KqXj2AaXxXXXXX","outcome":{"type":"authorized","risk_level":"normal"},"payment_method_details":{"card":{"brand":"visa","last4":"4242","checks":{"cvc_check":"fail","address_line1_check":"failed","address_postal_code_check":"pass"}}},"failure_message":"Your card's security code is incorrect.","failure_code":"incorrect_cvc"}
```
billing_country: US; customer submitted address: "123 Maple Ave, Apt 4B" vs PSP returned "123 Maple Avenue".

omar: Looks like both `cvc_check` failed and `address_line1_check` failed — classic AVS normalization mismatch. Could also be cardholder typed abbreviated street (St vs Street) or apt placement. Not a Redwood API issue, but we should help productize guidance.

payments-bot: webhook received for ch_3KqXj2AaXxXXXXX at 2026-03-17T15:42:10Z — decline reason: incorrect_cvc, avs_result: N (address mismatch).

sam: Repro request: can you try creating a minimal invoice and charging with a test token that simulates avs/cvc failures? Use our billing sandbox: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoices/INV-TEST/charge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-xxx" \
  -d 'card[number]=4000000000003220' \
  -d 'card[exp_month]=12' -d 'card[exp_year]=2025' -d 'card[cvc]=000' 
```
This token on PSP returns AVS/CVC mismatch in test mode.

maria: I ran that in sandbox — same response structure; invoice stays unpaid, webhook posted `card_declined`. I also pulled customer support transcript: they manually re-entered card and it worked second time (they corrected street suffix).

omar: Action items: 1) Support reply template recommending re-entry and small guidance on street formatting (e.g., use full word Avenue/Street), 2) Add a UI hint in billing page to show the canonical formatted address returned by the bank on decline (if available) so users can quickly see mismatch, 3) For recurring payments, offer to surface retry with updated card.

sam: For engineering: add logging to attach PSP's `checks` object to our invoice events (non-PHI-safe — ensure we mask PAN). Proposed event shape: `invoice.payment_failed` includes `psp_checks: {cvc_check, address_line1_check, postal_code_check}`. Any objections?

maria: +1 — helps support triage. Also request a short KB article: "Why my card was declined: AVS and CVV checks" with screenshots and sample phrasing for customers.

payments-bot: Created JIRA RED-2456 - "Surface PSP AVS/CVC checks in invoice failure events" and linked thread.

sam: One more: confirm tax/VAT edge cases — sometimes billing country mismatch triggers extra scrutiny; for now flag to payments team to check if `billing_country` vs `card_country` mismatches correlate with more AVS fails.

maria: I'll respond to customer with: apology, ask them to confirm address formatting exactly as on card, try re-typing CVC, and offer to accept a different payment method. Will escalate if declines persist. :pray:

omar: If customer is enterprise and we need to accept PO, remind Sales that PO path bypasses card network so avoids AVS/CVV.

maria: Closing loop — will update once customer confirms retry. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
